newsitem.title: UK: Middle East crude tankers stuck in doldrums.
newsitem.headline: Middle East crude tankers stuck in doldrums.

text.p: The key Middle East crude tanker market failed to revitalise after the very slow start this week with no VLCC business concluded.
Other lifting sectors were seen busier, while freight rates were broadly unchanged globally, brokers said.
"Activity in the Mideast Gulf is extremely poor and rates for VLCCs seem to possess a bearish downside at the moment," said one London broker.
But in the medium term rates could rise next week as tonnage was not viewed as oversupplied.
Western voyages could only command W50 whilst rates for VLCCs travelling East settled at W58.
VLCCs bound for Japan were placed at W60.
By mid-afternoon, Shell's chartering of the VLCC Golar Dundee, travelling to South Africa, was the only activity seen, brokers said.
Rates for 80,000 tonners going cross-Med stayed around W92.5-95 though as high as W102.5 was seen.
But OMV's chartering of the Tom at W102.5 was not seen typical of the market.
In the inter-UKC sector rates were consolidating with trendline support at W94, amid thicker activity.
A single transatlantic trip was seen, with BP taking the 80,000 tonner Teseo to the U.S. Gulf at W92.5.
Caribbean rates for 70,000 tonners heading upcoast U.S soared. Levels were up 12.5 Worldscale points at W140.
"Rates have risen due to a lack of vessels in the region. We should see them remain at this level for the next couple of days," a U.S. broker said.
